title: LLMs are bad at vibing specifications
summary: Hillel Wayne finds beginner-vibed TLA+ and Alloy specs often don't compile and check only tautological properties, so LLMs mainly help people who already know formal methods.

assertions.quote: The AI is only writing "obvious properties"

verdicts.note: Expert reviewers report this pattern repeatedly in AI-generated specs, but the evidence is anecdotal and models are improving.

assertions.quote: being easily able to write specifications doesn't help with correctness if the specs don't actually verify anything
If you need to know formal methods to get the LLM to do formal methods, is that really helping?
So we know the person did not actually run these specs.
It does not seem to be good at writing "subtle" properties that fail due to concurrency, nondeterminism, or bad behavior separated by several steps.
